name: Shoney

attributes.attribute: god of the sea honored on Lewis and Harris
received a mug of ale poured into the ocean at Samhain

sources: Spence, Lewis. The Minor Traditions of British Mythology. (New York: Benjamin Blom, Inc., 1972), 28.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Shoney is a Scottish god of the sea. Until the 1600s the folk of the Isle of Lewis and Harris honored him. He stayed obscure to the wider world. Each Samhain the fisher folk carried out a mug of ale. They poured it into the ocean. They called to Shoney to accept the mug. They asked him to fill their boats with fish. Some see him as the root of Davy Jones, the guide of the sailors. The rite kept a bond between the sea folk and the god who fed them.
